source_text: The BMA requires dual parental consent where feasible and highlights legal risks under child protection frameworks, but detractors argue this stance selectively discounts global epidemiological data on penile cancer prevention and sexually transmitted infection mitigation, potentially biasing toward cultural contexts with low disease prevalence.
